title: Object equality versus reference equality
context: What is the difference between == and equals()?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: `==` compares references for objects: it is true only when both variables point to the same object. For primitives it compares values. `equals()` is a method that a class can override to compare content. `Object.equals` defaults to `==`. Strings, boxed numbers and collections override `equals`. If you override `equals`, also override `hashCode`, so equal objects land in the same hash bucket.

points.title: == compares identity
points.why: Two equal strings created separately are different objects, so == returns false.

points.title: Override hashCode with equals
points.why: Hash-based collections break when equal objects have different hash codes.
